title: Chapter 221: The Wrong Scenario
html:
“I think we’re almost at the end. No wonder Boss Chen calls this place the Third Sick Hall—stay here long enough, and even a healthy person would go mad.”

“I wonder how the workers cope. Spending every day in a place this realistic, surrounded by all that deranged writing on the walls... Boss Chen must offer them counseling.”

“Now that you mention it, we’ve been in here for almost ten minutes, but we haven’t seen a single Haunted House worker.”

“Enough chatter. We’re coming to a corner. Watch out for anything that might jump at you.”

It had taken the visitors seven minutes to reach the end of the corridor. Keeping their backs to the wall, they peered around the corner—and froze. “Another corridor?”

The scene was almost identical: aged walls, a cracked floor, endless messages scrawled in blood, and dolls bundled inside mattresses. The only difference was that the colors on the walls had grown darker. Through the cracks, they could see shapes resembling blood vessels.

“A background loop?” Han Qiuming frowned as he stood at the corner, using a term unfamiliar to the others.

“You mean they’ve repeated the previous set?” Luoluo and Xiao Du had never heard the term before.

“It looks identical, but each repetition contains subtle changes you won’t notice. Then, when you’re at your most vulnerable, all the scares strike at once.”

Han Qiuming continued confidently, “I saw this at an overseas Haunted House called Recurring Nightmare. The entire scenario consisted of nine rooms, each more frightening than the last. Most importantly, the rooms could be rearranged at will, so whenever you opened a door, you had no idea what might have been added on the other side.”

“You’re talking about separate rooms, which are much easier to manipulate. Here, they’ve decorated an entire corridor the same way.” Guo Miao touched the wall and lowered his voice. “Everything feels authentic, as though Boss Chen moved a real mental hospital into the Haunted House. I can’t explain it, but I have a feeling that’s exactly what he did.”

“Old Guo, you’re being too sensitive.” Han Qiuming chuckled. “Ever since you returned from the hospital where Xu Zhenzhen killed herself, you’ve become a coward. We operate Haunted Houses; fear and terror are our livelihood. If you’re this frightened, how can you expect to scare anyone else?”

“Qiuming, I didn’t believe it at first either, but once you’ve dealt with these things a few more times, you’ll understand.”

“From where I’m standing, you’ve regressed.” Han Qiuming faced Guo Miao. “Honestly, how can you tolerate this after he brought your attraction down on its opening day? Do you know how much time and effort we put into preparing for that day? That Chen fellow ruined everything, yet you still think he’s a good man? You want a truce with him? Have you lost your mind, or are you going senile?”

“Qiuming, that wasn’t Boss’s fault,” Song An said in a low voice. “If anyone was at fault, it was you for changing the advertisement without warning. You insisted on calling us Jiujiang’s scariest Haunted House and belittled every other attraction in the city.”

“So now it’s my fault?” Han Qiuming’s expression darkened. “Tian Teng Medical School is the newest enclosed Haunted House I’ve designed, drawing on all my years of experience. It even has a hidden storyline. I admit there are things we can learn from this place, but compared with my design, it’s still juvenile.”

“I’m not arguing with you. You weren’t there that day, so you don’t understand what happened.”

“Had I been there, things would have ended differently. You’re Haunted House employees, yet a visitor frightened you out of your own attraction. You’ve become the laughingstock of the industry.” With a single remark, Han Qiuming had insulted every employee present, but he did not seem to care. “It looks like we’ll have to intensify your training when we get back.”

“Qiuming, we can discuss this later. We have other visitors with us.” Guo Miao ignored Han Qiuming’s barbs.

“Oh, we’ll certainly discuss it. Once we’re back, I need to speak with our sponsor. I think you’ve grown too old to run this business.”

Furious, Song An rounded on him. “Han Qiuming! Boss has shown you nothing but kindness. Don’t go too far!”

“I’ve gone too far? Every decision I’ve made has been for the Haunted House’s benefit. Tian Teng Medical School has undergone four redesigns, and I was responsible for three of them.” Han Qiuming chuckled. “You all know how effective they were.”

“You mean using a real case in the Haunted House and turning a dead victim’s name into a prop—then getting us sued? That’s what you call effective?”

“Sorry, but results are all that interest me. According to the data, ticket sales increased fivefold after we added the dead Xu Zhenzhen to the attraction.” Han Qiuming shrugged, as if he had every right to be proud. “I saved your careers. And remember, I’m the designer your sponsor begged to help you. You’re merely an employee of the Haunted House.”

“You exploited a real case and used a dead woman’s name to attract attention. While you were designing it, did you ever consider how the victim’s family might feel?”

“Now you’re turning on me? Why didn’t any of you object at the beginning?”

“Enough!” Guo Miao pulled Han Qiuming and Song An apart. “We can settle this when we return. Boss Chen cleared our Haunted House alone. If all of us together can’t clear his, that will be truly humiliating.”

Han Qiuming and Song An both seethed with anger, and for the moment, it overwhelmed their fear.

“Who has time to argue with someone like him?” Song An strode ahead alone.

“Old Song, don’t wander off by yourself!” Afraid something might happen to him, Guo Miao hurried after Song An, putting some distance between themselves and the rest of the group.

“The world really is full of all kinds.” Han Qiuming strolled along at the rear. The Third Sick Hall had shocked him when he first entered, but he was feeling much better now.

He glanced back. “You three, stay close to me. We have ten minutes left, but don’t worry—I’ll clear this scenario. This Haunted House might be impressive by domestic standards, but compared with the ones overseas, it’s nothing.”

“Mr. Han, I understand what you’re saying, but there’s something I need to confirm.” Xiao Du stood at the back of the group, his face blanched. He had paid no attention to the argument between Han Qiuming and Song An; something else had occupied him entirely.

“What is it?”

“Didn’t you say the mannequins wouldn’t get within five meters of us?”

Xiao Du pointed behind them. Every one of those unnervingly lifelike mannequins had entered the Third Sick Hall.

At their head stood the schoolgirl mannequin with the name tag. Her head hung low, and she was only three or four meters behind Xiao Du.
